metadata.focus: High-risk alternate event verification and duplicate-episode quarantine
metadata.notes: All five new evidence records are alternate-event occurrence/date/location cross-checks only. Institutionally related sources are explicitly disclosed; the duplicate flags require replacement, not automatic removal of research history.

alternate_reviews.title: A rare snow-and-ice event paralyzes central Alabama
alternate_reviews.location: Elmore County and the Birmingham–Montgomery corridor, Alabama
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: Snow and freezing rain affected central Alabama on January 28, 2014, with extensive road icing and hazardous travel; the selected NCEI Elmore County segment is one piece of that regional event.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NWS Birmingham provides contemporaneous local observation and impact records; a later peer-reviewed meteorological case study independently analyzes the episode but uses some of the same surface observations and reports.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Do not conflate January 28 conditions with January 29–30 impacts, assume all roads had equal icing, or treat one Elmore County row as statewide statistics. First-hand photos embedded in agency pages may be privately owned.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original January 28 warm-nose sounding/road-temperature timeline paired with verified local snow and ice reports.

alternate_reviews.title: An EF3 tornado strikes Columbus, Mississippi
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: A destructive EF3 tornado moved through Columbus, Mississippi, on February 23, 2019, as part of an evening severe-weather episode.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NWS Jackson tornado survey and NCEI local event entry derive from the same NOAA damage-assessment and storm-report system, so they corroborate the identity/date but do NOT independently verify EF-scale wind speeds or injury totals.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Source injury totals differ by account/reporting scope (NCEI individual segment versus NWS event summary); do not publish injuries or fatalities before direct/indirect and geographic reconciliation. EF3 is a surveyed damage rating, not a measured wind gust.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original survey-track and damage-indicator schematic showing EF3 location without assigning peak rating to every point along the track.

alternate_reviews.title: An F5 tornado devastates Lubbock, Texas
alternate_reviews.secondary_publisher: National Bureau of Standards (NIST historical archive)
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On May 11, 1970, a violent tornado devastated parts of Lubbock, Texas; federal Weather Bureau records and a National Bureau of Standards structural-damage survey document the event.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NWS/Weather Bureau chronology and a separately conducted National Bureau of Standards structural field survey provide complementary event evidence; both necessarily reference the same physical tornado, and F5 rating derives from damage analysis.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Use historical F-scale (F5), not modern EF5. Lubbock experienced more than one tornado that evening; distinguish first and destructive second tornado. Damage estimates, fatalities, and wind speeds require claim-specific archival reconciliation. Historic photographs have item-specific rights.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original 1970 Lubbock damage footprint and mapped Weather Bureau observation timeline from May 11.

alternate_reviews.title: Hurricane Gracie makes landfall on South Carolina's Lowcountry
alternate_reviews.location: St. Helena Island–Beaufort area, South Carolina
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: Hurricane Gracie made landfall near the South Carolina Lowcountry's St. Helena Island/Beaufort area on September 29, 1959; later official summaries classify it as a major hurricane.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: South Carolina state climatology's historical storm summary and NWS Charleston's regional tropical-cyclone history both date landfall to September 29; both use overlapping retrospective HURDAT, weather-observation, and historical archives.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: An older South Carolina historical summary lists Category 3, whereas modern state/NWS pages list Category 4. Distinguish retrospective intensity revisions from contemporary 1959 analysis and do not assert precise landfall point or instantaneous wind without a reviewed best track. Original HURDAT point had unverified geographic precision.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original reconstructed September 29 Lowcountry landfall track with dated tide/gauge and wind observations; separate historical from reanalyzed intensity.

alternate_reviews.title: An F4 tornado sweeps past Earlington, Kentucky
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: An F4 tornado touched down near Earlington, Kentucky, on November 15, 2005 and tracked toward the Hanson area, separate in time and geography from the November 1989 Huntsville tornado primary.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: Two NWS office archives independently present the tornado's date and geographic track but refer to the same underlying NWS/Storm Data damage survey. They are not independent F-scale intensity measurements.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Use F4 (pre-EF scale). Do not equate maximum F4 damage with intensity along the full path or conflate this Hopkins County tornado with other tornadoes in the November 15, 2005 outbreak. Historical tornado timing uses local CST.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original Earlington–Hanson damage-track map with local-time markers and an F4 segment highlighted.

duplicate_checks.scope: Newburgh, Indiana is a downstream segment of the same November 6, 2005 Evansville-area F3 tornado featured as primary
Houston airport flash flooding is within the same September 19, 2019 Tropical Storm Imelda episode as the primary
Woodland Terrace flash flooding is within the same October 4, 2015 South Carolina flood episode as the primary
A countywide Texas flash-flood entry is a segment of the same October 17, 1998 Central Texas flood primary
Schenectady ice is part of the same December 11–12, 2008 Northeastern ice storm as the primary
Gray County Texas wildfire is part of the same regional March 6, 2017 Plains wildfire outbreak as the primary; distinct ignition has not been verified, so this is not a defensible independent backup

editorial_deferrals.reason: Retired unverified offshore track marker in favor of documented September 29 Lowcountry landfall. Historical Category 3 versus retrospective Category 4 source discrepancy remains claim-level caution.
Lubbock 1970 tornado is separate from the Waco 1953 primary, but still shares tornado hazard; retained as scientifically interesting alternate pending visual/editorial diversity selection.
